summary: New stem I (nḏərre (3pl Preterit)/nəḏro (3sg.f Infectum); 3sg.m-Grundformen nicht gesichert)
example for sense 1 in Preterit-wa (MAC Besim History of Bsorino/51)

data.turoyo: Ŭ kul ʕáylaste obowa u+naʕimayḏa, u+bəkkər, l Mor+Gabriyèl, tamo d̥qore, dyolaf ŭ d̥owe dayroyo. Nuḏrólewa ltamo.
data.translation: And every family would give their child, their firstborn, to Mor Gabriel so that he could study there (lit. there so that he study), learn there and become a monk. It dedicated him to there.

rationale: First Preterit-wa evidence for dedicating a child; exact inflection remains an editorial question.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (PrS 6/10)

data.turoyo: Kul barṯo nḏəlla naḏro li ldaṯalo, kul ḥḏo dinoro.
data.translation: Jede ihrer Töchter gelobte der Mutter Gottes ein Gelübde, jede ein Goldstück.

rationale: First Preterit evidence; cognate object, sacred dedicatee and promised amount.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (Jan 2.15/3491)

data.turoyo: Xori Brahim: Hawən, nḏərre ruḥayye li xədme d Aloho, fayiši dayrəyoṯo, səmənne dayrəyoṯo.
data.translation: Father Brahim: They came to be; they dedicated themselves to God's service, remained nuns; they made them nuns.

rationale: Self as dedicated participant, extending the thin round-1 Preterit cell. English is verbatim project machine translation; semantic analysis rests on Turoyo.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (Jan 2.15/3495)

data.turoyo: Xori Brahim: Lo, lo, lo. Layto, tarix latle. E, hawxa masala, ḥḏo d nəḏro ruḥa, kəwyo dayrayto, d xədmo u qadišo.
data.translation: Father Brahim: No, no, no. There is none; it has no history. Yes, a matter like this: a woman who dedicates herself becomes a nun, to serve the saint.

rationale: Fills the still-thin round-1 vow/dedication sense; Infectum is newly attested in Jan. English is verbatim project machine translation; semantic analysis rests on Turoyo.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (Jan 2.15/3493)

data.turoyo: Aṯən ad dayroyoṯo mərre: "Aḥna amṭelan, nḏərlan ʕal ruḥayna, gədhəwena dayroyoṯo, xədmina u qadišo."
data.translation: The nuns came and said, "We have come, we have made a vow upon ourselves; we will become nuns and serve the saint."

rationale: First-person plural Preterit with ʕal ruḥayna; explicit undertaken religious service. English is verbatim project machine translation; semantic analysis rests on Turoyo.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (Jan 2.31/5059)

data.turoyo: Qay matrakke aš šahwat di arʕaṯe w nḏərre aḥ ḥayaṯṯe lə Mšiḥo?" D məftakər, d šuqele dars, čike maḥ ḥaye du qadišo yo, d əzzeyo li ʕito, haṯe yo.
data.translation: Why did they leave the desires of their earth and dedicate their lives to Christ?" So that he reflects, so that he should take a lesson from a little of the saint's life, so that he should go to church; that is it.

rationale: Lives as dedicated object and lə Mšiḥo dedicatee; fourth Preterit example after round 1. English is verbatim project machine translation; semantic analysis rests on Turoyo.

summary: Correct the readers’ absence claim: nḏr is already an etymologized entry stub with notes PrS 14/1 and to vow. The revision supplies a stem, sense and source examples rather than creating a duplicate root.

The theme can be a cognate naḏro with an amount and l-dedicatee, or a child resumed from the preceding clause with l-monastery/ltamo goal. Both express ritual commitment; no separate person-dedication sense is needed on present evidence.
The cognate noun naḏro does not itself prove a light verb with a semantically empty verb; keep it in the lexical sense rather than duplicate it in Idiomatic phrases.
The two observed forms are supplied as attested forms because the canonical Preterit/Infectum pair is not securely recoverable. No unobserved Infectum or masculine citation form has been invented.
Keep nḏr distinct from roof-rolling ndr and seeing nḏ̣r. The added I assignment is provisional pending a native paradigm; the two secure sacred-commitment contexts justify the lexical entry.
Jan English is project machine translation, not an edition translation. Senses rest on Turoyo alone; quoted English retains the supplied wording. This JSON contains only round-2 proposals.
The original glossary has an etymologized nḏr stub; round 1 already supplied stem I and lexical sense 1. Jan absence claims are outdated.
Jan nəḏro adds a feminine Infectum form to the previously incomplete paradigm. Display only attested person forms; no canonical masculine pair is reconstructed.
Active Preterit L-suffixes encode the dedicating participants, including the reflexive self-object construction; this is not a Detransitive.
The ʕal ruḥayna phrase does not establish a light-verb idiom or semantically distinct new sense; it expresses the bearer of the commitment.
Confirm stem I and the canonical Preterit/Infectum pair, including r+l assimilation in nḏəlla and the object, agent and -wa segmentation of Nuḏrólewa.
Does Nuḏrólewa resume the feminine household as agent or an impersonal donor? The preceding obowa is feminine; the later suffix sequence is not securely segmented.
What does the inherited PrS 14/1 stub reference point to? The assigned new vow passage is PrS 6/10; do not replace the unexamined inherited note.
Confirm the canonical Preterit/Infectum pair and the relation of nḏərre/nḏərlan to round-1 nḏəlla and Nuḏrólewa.
Does ʕal ruḥayna specifically mark a binding undertaking, and how does it differ pragmatically from the direct ruḥ- object?
Confirm the local nḏr spelling and its historical relation to Syriac ndr; no etymological rewrite is inferred here.
All four Jan passages support round-1 dedication, adding ruḥ- and life as themes, l- divine dedicatees, and ʕal ruḥayna for a commitment imposed upon oneself. No duplicate root or sense is proposed.
